clue.text: Handy tools for building bridges

parts.note: plain workshop tools, but the phrase also hints at things that stretch across a gap from one side to the other, as a bridge does

explanation.surface: A builder's kit list for a bridge-building job.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of engineering kit; the wit is that the word for these hand tools literally means things that stretch across, like bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: These adjustable wrenches are standard hand tools, and the word also suggests objects that cross a gap.

clue.text: Split if one's married after school?

indicators.note: the married and one's pieces come after the school piece in the finished word

parts.note: one's read as I'S, the numeral one plus the possessive S
M is the abbreviation for married in records and genealogies

explanation.surface: A question about whether a marriage straight out of school causes a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' must be read as I'S, numeral plus possessive; 'after' sets the later pieces behind the school abbreviation. The surface's 'Split' looks like a verb but defines a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, especially a church.

clue.text: Sailor lies about descent

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word lies are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaman tells tall tales about a descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives SEIL; 'lies' looks like a verb in the surface but is only fodder, and AB is the stock crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abseil is a controlled descent down a rope on a cliff or wall.

clue.text: Public official's negative article on the railway

parts.note: not is a negative word
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A railway bureaucrat makes a pedantic grammatical point.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public officer who witnesses signatures and certifies documents.

clue.text: Withdrawal when about to get a grip

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
traction is the grip of a tyre or wheel on a surface

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out just as they are about to get a grip on things.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction is the taking back or withdrawal of a statement.

clue.text: A Spanish gentleman is a man admired

parts.note: Don is the Spanish courtesy title for a gentleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman is widely admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Adonis, the beautiful youth of Greek myth, now names any strikingly handsome man.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a very handsome young man, one who draws admiration for his looks.

clue.text: Rant from the clan supports raising assistance

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below, so the clan piece comes underneath
in a down clue raising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: aid means assistance
a tribe is a clan

explanation.surface: A tribal leader rails while the clan helps raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns AID upwards to DIA; 'supports' puts TRIBE beneath it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful rant.

clue.text: Able to figure out menu — and the price!

indicators.note: out signals the letters of menu are put out of order

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A diner who can work out the menu and its cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' gives NUME. 'figure' here means to do sums, not to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone numerate is competent with numbers and arithmetic.

clue.text: Africans litigate against accepting Europeans

indicators.note: accepting means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: to sue is to litigate against someone
Danes are Europeans from Denmark

explanation.surface: Africans take Europeans to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' signals the container; 'litigate against' is one phrase for a single verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sudanese are the people of Sudan, a country in Africa.

clue.text: Pause when breaking ties in extreme dislike

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the dislike word

parts.note: hate is extreme dislike

indicators.note: breaking signals that the letters of ties are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone holds back when breaking off relationships out of loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' gives ESIT and 'in' places it after the first letter of the dislike word; 'ties' suggests relationships but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause before acting, out of doubt.

clue.text: Worked the land a long way from the sea

parts.note: far means a long way
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A farmer who tilled soil far inland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; the surface suggests distance from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that was farmed was cultivated or tilled.

clue.text: Solid par round gives access to fast track!

indicators.note: round signals that the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's steady par round puts them on the fast track to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges SOLIDPAR. 'fast track' is a motorway; this road leads onto or off it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is a short road for joining or leaving a motorway, the fast route.

clue.text: Practice for TT race?

parts.note: TT looks like the Isle of Man motorbike race but also means teetotal, so the practice is one where nobody drinks

explanation.surface: A rider's warm-up lap before the Isle of Man TT motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man TT is a famous motorcycle race; TT also stands for teetotal, i.e. alcohol-free.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal before the real thing; here also a race practice without alcohol.

clue.text: Eloquent, like Lucretia at work

indicators.note: work as a verb means knead or reshape, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A compliment on how well-spoken a woman called Lucretia is at her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the ten letters of LUCRETIAAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An articulate speaker expresses ideas clearly and fluently.

clue.text: Characteristics of butter as it melts

indicators.note: melting changes shape, so these letters lose their order and reform

explanation.surface: A description of how butter behaves as it softens in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melts' rearranges the ten letters of BUTTERASIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Attributes are qualities or features belonging to something.

clue.text: Shows nervousness seeing the Yorkshire charmers

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
witches cast charms and spells

explanation.surface: Someone visibly jumpy on meeting enchantresses from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t', as in 'down t'pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who twitches makes small jerky movements, a sign of being nervous.

clue.text: Made money — that's apt in professional journalist!

indicators.note: in places the apt piece inside the professional journalist pair

parts.note: pro is short for professional
ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist
fit means apt or suitable

explanation.surface: A remark that it is fitting for a career journalist to have earned well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the apt word between the two abbreviations; 'that's' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have profited is to have gained financially, earned a return.

clue.text: Key service elevator needs renovation

parts.note: F is a musical key
an ace is a winning serve in tennis
lift is the British word for an elevator

explanation.surface: A lift engineer's report that the main elevator needs a refit.
explanation.walkthrough: An ace is a tennis serve the receiver cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic renovation, of a face or figuratively of a building.

clue.text: How air-lock is fixed by one whose job matters most?

indicators.note: fixed here means repaired or redone, so the letters are put back together differently

explanation.surface: A question of who will repair the air-lock: a person who lives for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fixed' rearranges the ten letters of HOWAIRLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A person addicted to their work puts their job above everything else.

clue.text: Listen to case of trespass suit

parts.note: hear means listen to

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A court asked to hear a trespass lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives T and S, the first and last letters of trespass. 'suit' is the card suit, not a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Animal rights initially supporting tag

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: a badge is a tag worn for identification

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word rights

explanation.surface: A campaign tag for animal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R from rights, which goes beneath BADGE as 'supporting' requires in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger is a burrowing nocturnal mammal with a striped face.

clue.text: Stopped seeing comfort in the Diplomatic Corps

indicators.note: in puts the comfort piece within the diplomats' abbreviation

parts.note: CD stands for Corps Diplomatique, the diplomatic corps
ease means comfort

explanation.surface: Diplomats no longer enjoy their comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: CD, from French Corps Diplomatique, appears on diplomats' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means came to an end, halted.

clue.text: Sweet but posh bloke with bearing and energy

parts.note: toff is British slang for an upper-class man
E, east, is a compass bearing
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Praise for an upper-class chap with fine manners and plenty of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a confection. A toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, a sweet made from boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Key employment left to mature body

parts.note: F is a musical key
use means employment, as in the employment of a tool
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: An instruction for ageing a body properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' is the main body of an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aeroplane, holding crew and passengers.

clue.text: Books absorbed in shock rhetoric

indicators.note: absorbed in means held inside, so the books piece goes within the shock piece

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
OT, Old Testament, is the crossword abbreviation for a set of books

explanation.surface: Readers deeply engrossed in books of shocking rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a thick mop of hair, not a surprise; OT goes after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty talk meant to impress is dismissed as overblown rhetoric with no substance.

clue.text: Shows anger after counter attacks

indicators.note: after puts the anger piece behind the counter piece

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub
rages means shows anger

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over the counter and lashes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' is a pub bar, not someone opposing.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrages are heavy bombardments or concentrated attacks.

clue.text: Calm corner of England before engagement

indicators.note: before places the corner piece ahead of the engagement piece

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a corner of England
a date is an engagement or appointment

explanation.surface: Someone from the south-east keeps cool ahead of a romantic engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried, composed.

clue.text: Made sure foul was deliberate

indicators.note: foul suggests something messed up, so these letters are fouled into a new order

explanation.surface: A referee confirms that a foul was intentional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' rearranges MADESURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured steps or words are careful and considered, done deliberately.
